200.title: German troops, martial law: Disinfo over top court drama floods Polish net
200.summary: Many of the images circulating on social media were AI-generated manipulations or deepfakes Polish cybersecurity specialists have identified close to 10,000 instances of disinformation spread through social media concerning a high-profile political crisis involving the country’s Constitutional Tribunal.
200.body: Many of the images circulating on social media were AI-generated manipulations or deepfakes Polish cybersecurity specialists have identified close to 10,000 instances of disinformation spread through social media concerning a high-profile political crisis involving the country’s Constitutional Tribunal. The dramatic scenes also fueled widespread online disinformation narratives, including false claims of martial law in Poland and the presence in the country of German police and soldiers. Other social media posts claimed that German riot police had been deployed outside the Constitutional Tribunal’s Warsaw HQ and that German soldiers had been sent to Poland. The riot officers were in fact Polish, PAP determined, while footage of German soldiers in Poland was unrelated to the events at the Constitutional Tribunal.

200.body: Polish deputy PM proposes “constitutional reset” to resolve crisis around top court Nov 6, 2026 | Law , Politics Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! The leader of one of the parties in Poland’s ruling coalition has put forward plans for a “constitutional reset” that he hopes can resolve the crisis around the country’s top court. The proposal, presented on Thursday by deputy prime minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, head of the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), would remove all current judges on the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) and allow new judges to be chosen only with the approval of 60% of members of parliament and the president.

500.title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman reacts to Delaware’s AI agent proposal, says it is ‘deeply concerning t
500.summary: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has warned against a legislative proposal in Delaware that would permit autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents to legally manage and operate corporate entities.
500.body: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has warned against a legislative proposal in Delaware that would permit autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents to legally manage and operate corporate entities. Suleyman pushed back the state’s initiative, saying that granting legal corporate status to autonomous software demands extreme scrutiny, and calling it ‘deeply concerning’. Quoting directly from the framework's core premise, Suleyman highlighted the far-reaching nature of the concept:“A Delaware AIC will be a separate legal entity whose day-to-day affairs are managed by an AI agent rather than a person. At the agent’s direction, the AIC can sue and be sued in its own name, hold and dispose of property, and incur obligations...”What is Delaware Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC)Delaware, widely recognised as America’s premier hub for corporate incorporations, is exploring a new business structure titled an Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC).
